references.text: Jesus emphasizes that he does not seek glory from people, but that true glory comes from God alone, a theme he further develops here when he says that his own glory is nothing without the Father.
At this moment, the Father's voice is heard from heaven to honor the Son's name, confirming that it is the Father who gives glory to the Son, just as Jesus claims in John 8:54.
Jesus asks the Father to glorify him with the glory he had with the Father before the world existed, showing that glory comes from the Father and is not something Jesus took for himself.
The psalm proclaims that glory should not belong to man, but only to God's name, a principle Jesus confirms when he says that his own glory is nothing without the Father.
God says that he will not give his glory to another, emphasizing that glory belongs to God alone, and that Jesus, as the Father's representative, receives this glory from him.
Jesus warns against those who seek their own glory, contrasting this with the one who seeks glory from the one who sent him, a theme directly parallel to the statement in John 8:54.
